🏉 AFL Fantasy Brownlow
🏆 Leaderboard
🏆 Leaderboard & Brownlow Votes
AFL Fantasy Brownlow simulates the Brownlow Medal using Fantasy scores — the top 3 scorers in each game each round receive 3, 2 and 1 votes respectively.

Columns explained:
  • Current Price — the player's current AFL Fantasy price.
  • Avg FP — average Fantasy Points scored per round played.
  • Total FP — cumulative Fantasy Points across all rounds loaded.
  • Votes — total simulated Brownlow votes. Ties broken by Total FP.
Click any player name to jump to their full stats in the Player Stats tab.

🛡 Matchup Difficulty
🛡 Matchup Difficulty Rating
Historical tab: How do players score vs their own average when facing each team? Rating 100 = league average. Above 100 = easier.

Upcoming Fixture tab: Predicted avg pts your players will score in each upcoming game, based on the opponent's historical concede rating. Weighted so closer games count more.

💰 Trading Centre
Plan trades and compare the stats impact side by side.

  • Enter your available budget ($K), then search to add players to Trade In / Trade Out.
  • Player chips show position, avg FP, last 3 avg, and form rating for quick comparison.
  • The Summary panel shows how the trade changes your avg FP and budget position.
  • Bookmarks: star any player in Player Stats to quick-add them here.

      🏉 My Team Analyser
      Add your 22-player squad. Players go into their position groups — DEF, MID, RUC, FWD — with the last 4 in each being bench (shaded). Add up to 30 players total.

      Click Analyse for ranked upgrade suggestions with trade pairs, using form, fixture, value, consistency, and bench context. Each card shows signal, avg FP, price trend, fixture, and best available replacement.

      🏆 Rolling 22 — Best Projected Team
      🏆 Rolling 22
      Shows the best projected 22-man AFL Fantasy team from your loaded data, laid out in DEF/MID/RUC/FWD formation.

      Overall — ranked by season avg FP. Form-weighted — last-3 avg vs price value. Fixture-adjusted — projected scores using upcoming opponent difficulty ratings.

      Players only appear once (their primary position is used). Bench spots show the next-best available.
